subject: science
skillName: Slowing Wind and Water from Changing the Land
intro: Wind and water can change the shape of the land by moving soil and sand away, which is called erosion. People design solutions to slow or prevent this. Plants and trees have roots that hold soil in place, walls and barriers can block moving water or wind, and rows of trees called windbreaks slow the wind. When there is more than one solution, we can compare them to see which one best slows or prevents the wind or water from changing the land.

items.prompt: A hill keeps losing soil when it rains because water washes it away. Planting grass with roots is one solution. How does this slow the change to the land?

steps: Water washing away soil changes the shape of the land.
Grass roots hold the soil in place so the water cannot carry it away as easily.
So planting grass slows the water from changing the land.
solution.answer: The grass roots hold the soil in place, so the water washes away less soil and the land changes more slowly.

items.prompt: Two solutions are compared to stop wind from blowing away sand: a row of trees (a windbreak) and doing nothing. Which works better and why?

steps: Wind blowing sand away changes the land.
A windbreak of trees slows the wind so it carries away less sand.
Doing nothing lets the wind keep blowing the sand, so the windbreak works better.
solution.answer: The windbreak works better, because the trees slow the wind so it blows away less sand, while doing nothing does not help.

items.prompt: Why do people compare more than one solution for protecting the land?

steps: There is often more than one way to slow wind or water.
Comparing the solutions shows which one slows or prevents the change best.
So comparing helps people choose the most effective solution.
solution.answer: Because comparing solutions shows which one best slows or prevents the wind or water from changing the land.

items.prompt: Name one solution that can slow water from washing away soil.

steps: Solutions hold soil in place or block the water.
Planting plants with roots (or building a wall) can slow water from washing soil away.
solution.answer: Planting plants with roots (or building a wall or barrier).

items.prompt: A beach is losing sand to waves. Two solutions are a rock wall and planting beach grass. How could each help?

steps: The waves are washing away the sand, changing the beach.
A rock wall blocks the waves so they carry away less sand.
Beach grass has roots that hold the sand in place, so both solutions slow the sand loss.
solution.answer: A rock wall blocks the waves and beach grass roots hold the sand, so both slow the loss of sand.

items.prompt: One solution slows erosion a lot and one barely helps. How would you decide which solution is better?

steps: The goal is to slow or prevent the wind or water from changing the land.
Compare how much each solution slows the erosion.
The solution that slows the erosion more is the better one.
solution.answer: Compare how much each slows the erosion, and choose the one that slows it more.
